title: Projection formula, integer coefficients
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
proper morphism, let
$E\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ have
torsion cohomology, and let
$K\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$. Then the canonical projection-formula map

$$
\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K):\quad
Rf_*E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}K\longrightarrow
Rf_*(E\kunotimes{\mathbf Z}f^{-1}K)
$$

is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$.

proof.text: Choose $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ such that $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i<a$ and $\mathcal H^j(K)=0$ for $j<b$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives the same bound $b$ for $f^{-1}K$. Set $F=E\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}f^{-1}K$. By [lem-kun-integral-derived-tensor-bounded-torsion], $F$ vanishes below $a+b-1$ and has torsion cohomology. The direct-image bound [lem-kun-tensor-t-est] gives $Rf_*E\in D^{\ge a}$ and $Rf_*F\in D^{\ge a+b-1}$. Applying the tensor bound once more, now to $Rf_*E$ and $K$ without the optional torsion clause, puts the source $Rf_*E\otimes^L K$ in $D^{\ge a+b-1}$ as well. Thus both sides lie in $D^+(Y_{\Et})$, and bounded-below torsion proper base change is applicable to both $E$ and $F$.

Fix an arbitrary geometric point $g:s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, and form the cartesian square with $Z=X\times_Ys$, $g':Z\to X$ and $h:Z\to s$. Properness is stable under this base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $h$ is separated and of finite type, so $Z$ is quasi-compact since $s$ is affine. To check quasi-separatedness as an absolute scheme, take affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U\times_s V=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_\Omega B)$. The inverse image of this open by the closed diagonal of $h$ is $U\cap V$, hence is $\operatorname{Spec}((A\otimes_\Omega B)/I)$ for an ideal $I$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ring map $A\otimes_{\mathbf Z}B\to A\otimes_\Omega B$ is surjective: it is the quotient imposing $(\lambda a)\otimes b=a\otimes(\lambda b)$. Consequently the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ has quasi-compact inverse image $U\cap V$ on every affine open $U\times_{\mathbf Z}V$ of this cover. It is quasi-compact, so $Z$ is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Thus $Z$ is qcqs, without any finiteness hypothesis on $Y$.

Write $E_s=(g')^{-1}E$ and $K_s=g^{-1}K$. The bounded-below proper base-change theorem [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] applied to $E$ and to $F$ makes both exchange morphisms $g^{-1}Rf_*E\to Rh_*E_s$ and $g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rh_*(g')^{-1}F$ isomorphisms. The hypotheses on $F$ were proved in Step 1. Inverse-image monoidality [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], together with $fg'=gh$, identifies $(g')^{-1}F$ with $E_s\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}h^{-1}K_s$, and identifies the pulled-back source with $g^{-1}Rf_*E\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}K_s$. The commuting square of [lem-kun-proj-formula-natural], for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, therefore identifies $g^{-1}\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K)$ through these isomorphisms with $\mathrm{PF}_h(E_s,K_s)$. This uses the canonical exchange morphisms, so it identifies the map, not only its two objects. On these bounded-below objects, the exchange used here and the unbounded exchange in the naturality square coincide: [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] both define the mate of the same composite $h^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*L\xrightarrow{\theta} (g')^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*L\xrightarrow{(g')^{-1}\varepsilon_f}(g')^{-1}L$, for $L=E,F$. The units and counits restrict to the same adjunction on the full bounded-below subcategories, so uniqueness of the adjoint transpose identifies these morphisms.

By [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], $K_s$ is the stalk complex of $K$. Apply [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] to the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ of Step 2. With $S_D$ its exact geometric-stalk equivalence, put $M=S_DK_s$. The lemma gives $K_s\cong C_sM$ and preserves the lower bound of $K_s$, so $M\in D^+(\mathbf Z)$. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] also gives $E_s\in D^+(Z_{\Et})$.

For $h:Z\to s$, [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-sections-adjunction] supplies the natural isomorphism $\beta:S_D Rh_*\cong R\Gamma(Z,-)$, using the canonical comparison $h^{-1}C_s\cong C_Z$. Its stated counit identity identifies the derived constant-section adjunction with the composite of the geometric-point equivalence and $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$. Thus these are the specified canonical identifications for $E_s$ and $E_s\otimes^L h^{-1}C_sM$, without a choice of an abstract isomorphism of their objects.

Apply the commuting square of [lem-kun-geometric-point-projection-comparison] to $E_s$ and $M$. Its vertical arrows are exactly the comparisons of the preceding step. The scheme $Z$ is qcqs by Step 2, and $E_s,M$ are bounded below by Step 4. Hence [lem-kun-0f0e] makes its bottom arrow $R\Gamma(Z,E_s)\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}M\to R\Gamma(Z,E_s\otimes^L_{\mathbf Z}C_ZM)$ an isomorphism. The square gives that $S_D\mathrm{PF}_h(E_s,C_sM)$ is an isomorphism. The equivalence of [lem-kun-geometric-point-derived-constants] reflects isomorphisms, and naturality in $K_s\cong C_sM$ identifies this with the desired assertion that $\mathrm{PF}_h(E_s,K_s)$ is an isomorphism.

Steps 3–6 show that the projection map is an isomorphism after inverse image to every geometric point of $Y$. Since the stalk at a geometric point is the inverse image along it [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback], exactness of geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] identifies the stalk of each cohomology morphism $\mathcal H^i(\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K))$ with the $i$th cohomology of this stalk map. It is therefore an isomorphism at every geometric stalk. By [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] each cohomology morphism is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. The cone then has zero cohomology in every degree, hence is zero in the derived category, proving that the original canonical map is invertible.

tool_uses.why: Exact constant-coefficient inverse image gives the lower bounds for pulled-back complexes; this unit has only the inverse-image definition, not its exactness theorem.

Geometric stalks detect sheaf isomorphisms, used after taking every cohomology sheaf; this is a generic etale-sheaf tool.
